android-mobile.name: Android Mobile
known_gaps: PSN account extraction is manual redirect-link handling, not silent OAuth.
Live OCR samples frames; Arabic OCR uses a bundled Tesseract model but accuracy is not validated on devices.
Long-duration A/V synchronization and device stability are not proven by source tests.

Phone-to-TV has local unencrypted ws:// and HTTP paths by default. Exact Origin allowlisting and trusted WSS endpoints are supported, but require deployment configuration and a trusted reverse proxy; the proxy-to-phone hop remains cleartext.

android-tv.name: Android TV
known_gaps: Manifest enables cleartext traffic for local ws:// transport. Exact Origins are enforced when supplied at build time; a TLS listener and certificate identity are not built into the app and require a trusted reverse proxy.
A/V synchronization and long-session decoder stability require more than structural/unit tests.

google-tv.name: Google TV
known_gaps: A separate Android APK module exists; device/emulator compatibility and target-specific behavior are not established by source presence.
Google TV codec, remote-control, and lifecycle compatibility remain unproven.

fire-tv.name: Amazon Fire TV
known_gaps: A separate Android APK module exists; Fire OS device compatibility is not established by source presence.
Fire TV codec, remote-control, and lifecycle compatibility remain unproven.

tizen.name: Samsung Tizen
known_gaps: AVPlay/HLS adapter and WSS-capable protocol client exist, but complete playback/audio behavior and packaged-app Origin behavior are not proven on a supported Tizen device.
Vendor package build/sign/install and long-session A/V sync are not evidenced by this source audit.

webos.name: LG webOS
known_gaps: HTML media/HLS adapter and WSS-capable protocol client exist, but complete playback/audio behavior and packaged-app Origin behavior are not proven on a supported webOS device.
IPK build/sign/install and long-session A/V sync are not evidenced by this source audit.

roku.name: Roku
known_gaps: SceneGraph/BrightScript HLS receiver is a prototype.
No complete audio pipeline or A/V synchronization implementation is evidenced by current Roku source.
Package build/sign/device validation are not evidenced by source presence.

xbox-edge.name: Xbox Edge
known_gaps: This is a browser receiver, not a native Xbox application.
WSS and same-origin HTTPS HLS proxy paths are supported; device-level A/V synchronization and long-session stability are not proven.

web.name: Web Browser
known_gaps: WSS and same-origin HTTPS HLS proxy paths are supported; browser/device HLS decoding, autoplay behavior, A/V synchronization and long-session stability are not proven.

playstation.name: PlayStation via Chiaki-NG
known_gaps: The supported route is Android Mobile + pinned Chiaki-NG Remote Play + phone-side PS Link relay; no native PS4/PS5 application is claimed.
Android CI must complete bootstrap and Gradle compilation, then the PS console/phone/TV path must be tested on hardware.

findings.summary: The overlay assumed fixed indentation and older caption-clear message shapes. Bootstrap failed first on the OCR timestamp and then on valid caption-clear calls carrying sessionId. The patch now accepts the current forms, preserves session IDs, and is idempotent.
findings.evidence: GitHub Actions run 45481552752 failed before Gradle. Full bootstrap now succeeds on repeated local runs; focused overlay regression tests pass.

findings.summary: Phone and TV servers still bind cleartext ws:// and HTTP on the LAN by default; there is no in-app TLS listener or server certificate identity. Pairing attempts are throttled and browser Origins are checked against an exact build-time allowlist. Android and browser clients support trusted WSS endpoints through a reverse proxy, but the proxy-to-phone hop remains cleartext unless separately protected.
findings.evidence: PairingAttemptLimiter applies to TV WebSocket auth and phone WebSocket/Roku HTTP auth. Exact-source success clears only that exact source; overflow-bucket success is intentionally a no-op, so hash collisions may cause collateral throttling but cannot clear accumulated failures. Overflow buckets are bounded by maxTrackedSources and expire under the rolling window. JVM regression smoke verifies collision isolation, alternating-source lockout, the map bound, and expiry. OriginAllowlist covers WebSocket, Roku pairing HTTP, and HLS routes. Do not expose port 8765 or claim end-to-end TLS.

findings.summary: The HLS AAC source is Android Playback Capture and depends on Android 10+, permission, and source-app capture policy. It is not the native Chiaki decoded-game-audio callback. Synthetic AAC tests verify muxing, not PS5 audio capture; device evidence is absent.
findings.evidence: The separate Chiaki PCM bridge is source-patched but native audio capture is not demonstrated; prior CI failure was before APK creation and no PS5/device test is available.

findings.summary: Arabic OCR now has three generated image samples covering font weight, size, background, and contrast. This is a narrow synthetic check, not game-scene accuracy or Android performance validation. Model provenance and redistribution terms still need confirmation.
findings.evidence: Local Tesseract 5.5.4 sample test passed; physical-device OCR remains NOT TESTED.

findings.summary: No platform has complete acceptance evidence: APK/WGT/IPK/Roku packaging, installation, real pairing, audio/video, A/V sync, long-session stability, security, and physical-device evidence remain incomplete.
findings.evidence: Acceptance matrix records 0/10 fully accepted platforms; browser and vendor receiver tests are simulated.

findings.summary: The upstream native OAuth client embeds a client credential in the APK. It is extractable and must not be treated as a server-side secret. User passwords and account tokens are not intended to be persisted or logged.
findings.evidence: Credential value intentionally omitted from the audit report.

findings.summary: Four shell scripts used a machine-specific Termux interpreter path and could not be launched directly on Linux. Their shebangs now use env bash.
findings.evidence: All tracked shell scripts pass bash -n.

findings.summary: The Android TV receiver accepted v2 pairing but did not answer application-level heartbeat messages, causing compatible browser receivers to treat a live session as stalled. It now validates the protocol version and replies with HEARTBEAT_ACK.
findings.evidence: The cross-platform regression suite and v2 protocol source tests pass; Android compilation remains blocked by the missing SDK.

findings.summary: The media sender used an untagged queue and could send stale packets through a replacement WebSocket; it also lacked bounded retry after transient disconnects. Queue entries now carry socket/generation identity, transitions are synchronized, and capped reconnect stops on manual disconnect.
findings.evidence: Cross-platform regression tests and media-state source checks pass; Android/Kotlin compilation could not be run without an Android SDK.

findings.summary: A temporarily unavailable MediaCodec input buffer incorrectly forced the decoder to wait for a new keyframe, potentially freezing video until the next IDR. The transient no-buffer path now drops only that sample; actual invalid-buffer handling still requests keyframe recovery.
findings.evidence: The focused regression contract passes; physical decoder behavior remains untested.

findings.summary: The PixelCopy cancellation callback used a three-argument lambda incompatible with the resolved kotlinx.coroutines API, preventing mobile Kotlin compilation. It now accepts the Throwable callback parameter and still releases the bitmap on cancellation.
findings.evidence: GitHub Actions run 45504723970 reported the type mismatch at this callback. The local compiler dependency is Android SDK/Gradle configuration, so the complete mobile build has not yet been rerun against this worktree.

findings.summary: Protocol v2 messages were not consistently bound to active sessions: mobile media_config lacked the ID, receiver servers accepted some stale controls/binary frames, and browser clients did not bind ACKs or heartbeats to their connection. The Android sender, three TV servers, phone server, and web/Tizen/webOS/Xbox clients now issue and enforce per-connection session IDs, including reconnect rebind and session-bound READY/ACK/stream URL messages.
findings.evidence: Cross-platform JS lifecycle tests and Python source contracts verify authenticated session IDs, stale READY/stream rejection, media_config rebinding, server ACK identity, and active-socket binary guards. Android compile remains blocked locally by the missing SDK.

findings.summary: The phone-side WebSocket server authenticated browser receivers by pairing code but did not require a connection session ID; broadcasts were not scoped to the receiver connection. It now stores a per-socket session ID, rejects mismatched heartbeat frames, and tags READY, subtitle, and HLS URL messages for each recipient.
findings.evidence: Python source contracts check session binding and per-client stream URL generation; browser tests validate READY, stream URL, subtitle, ACK, heartbeat, WSS, and HTTPS HLS routing.

github_actions_evidence.stage: Gradle bootstrap passed; mobile Kotlin compilation failed on the PixelCopy cancellation callback and the not-yet-added sessionId field. APK build steps were not reached.
Web receiver protocol and HLS adapter tests.

scope_note: The inventory records existence, type, size, and SHA-256 for tracked and non-ignored untracked worktree files. It is not a per-file functional review or vendor-device certification; review findings and test evidence are separately recorded, and no 100% completion claim is made.
